meta.source: research round 2026-09-14 — the EU classification-and-statute layer. Thomas: “read the handoff, i want to move to The EU classification-and-statute layer.”
meta.note:
EU CLASSIFICATION-AND-STATUTE LAYER, FIRST ROUND. RESULT: 5 nodes, 75 dependencies, 4 dropped notes.

CONTINUED THE SAME DAY, and the continuation opens by correcting this file. The three edges at the END of `dependencies` — `nace-rev2 -> isic`, `cpa -> nace-rev2`, `eurostat-prodcom -> eu-combined-nomenclature` — all come from ONE document, Eurostat's own NACE Rev. 2 volume (KS-RA-07-015-EN), which the first pass wrote off as 'a 10-page cover extract'. It is 369 pages: `file` misreports that PDF's page count and `pdfinfo` does not, and the first pass believed `file`. The volume states the NACE-to-ISIC derivation under its own heading, states the CPA-to-NACE relationship that the CPA's own establishing regulation never mentions, and states where the Prodcom list's headings come from. The `nace-rev2 -> isic` dropped note below is kept and marked `resolved` rather than deleted, with the mistake written into it.

WHAT WAS THIN AND WHY THIS IS THE FIX. The EU-level instruments were the least-wired part of a well-wired region: `esa-2010` carried 116 in-edges while `nace-rev2` carried 2, `cpa` 1, `eu-reg-223-2009` 2 and `eu-reg-2019-2152` 1 — i.e. the corpus documented the EU's ACCOUNTING framework thoroughly and its CLASSIFICATION and STATUTE framework hardly at all. ECOICOP, the classification every HICP in the European Statistical System is broken down by, had no node at all, and `eurostat-hicp` — a 26-out-edge hub — had no legal basis recorded. This round mints the ECOICOP node and the three acts that set it, and wires the member-state side.

THE ROUTE, AND THE PART WORTH REUSING. EUR-Lex answers this container with an AWS WAF challenge — HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body — on every legal-content URL tried, with or without a browser User-Agent. CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository, serves the same acts: `http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` with an `Accept-Language: eng` header, which REDIRECTS to a `resource/cellar/<uuid>.<seq>/DOC_1` document that a plain GET then reads with no header at all. The cited URL is that resolved one, deliberately, because that is what a later grader run will issue. A bare `celex/` URL without the header returns an error stub, and with a plain Accept returns RDF metadata rather than the text — neither would have graded. Older acts (1059/2003, 3924/91) have no xhtml expression and need `Accept: text/html`.

THE MEMBER-STATE SIDE. Eurostat's national HICP reference metadata — PLAYBOOK-CORPUS rule 16's route — carries the answer twice on one page: section 3.2 'Classification system' names ECOICOP, and section 6.1 'Institutional Mandate - legal acts and other agreements' names Regulation (EU) 2016/792 and says what it does. Thirty countries, two edges each, one fetch each. The filename list in `notes/techniques-2026-09-04.md` is PARTLY STALE and was re-probed rather than trusted: AT, BE, DE, FR, IE, LU, NL, PT and SE are all `hi4` and none of them was in that note's `hi4` list; FI is `hi3`, as the note already says. Full current split in the round's notes file.

TWO THINGS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. (1) Section 6.1 is COMMON TEMPLATE TEXT, word for word across all 31 pages read. It is still the country's own reference metadata — section 1.1 names the national statistical institute as contact organisation, and it is the same document class the 2026-09-05 weights pass already wired 26 of these nodes off — but 30 edges resting on one paragraph shape is a concentration an audit should be told about rather than left to discover, so every one of those bases says so. Section 3.2 varies between the two templates and is not in that class. (2) The quote spans are cut at text-node boundaries, not at sentence boundaries. On the newer template 'The HICP uses the' sits outside the `<a>` that carries the classification name; on the older one the field has no sentence at all. The classification name alone is the span present in both, so that is the span, and every one of the 72 quotes in this slice was checked against the exact bytes a plain GET returns, through a local reimplementation of the grader's own `stripHtml`/`normalizeForMatch` pipeline, BEFORE the slice was written.

RULE 11's URL TRAP IS LIVE HERE. 68 already-live edges cite the 27 Eurostat metadata URLs this round also cites — the 2026-09-05 weights pass and the `eurostat-hicp` fan-in. Any future `grade-evidence` run touching these URLs must pass the OLD edges and the NEW ones together to `--edges`, or it will rewrite each URL's `evidence-cache/` record to hold only the ones it selected. The full list is in `notes/eu-classification-statute-2026-09-14.md`.

WHAT WAS REFUSED. `nace-rev2 -> isic` and `cpa -> cpc` both looked available and neither was taken — see the dropped notes. Germany and Türkiye are the two countries whose ESMS page was read and whose edge was NOT wired, because the corpus node is the national CPI and the page describes the HICP.

reports.title: European classification of individual consumption according to purpose (ECOICOP)
title_aliases: European Classification of Individual Consumption according to Purpose
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The consumption classification every HICP in the European Statistical System is broken down by, set out in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2016/792 and replaced by ECOICOP version 2 under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3159, applied to the full series from the January 2026 publication. Eurostat's own HICP metadata states that ECOICOP version 2 is identical to the UN's 2018 classification down to the 5-digit level. Minted 2026-09-14 in the EU classification-and-statute round.
reports.cadence_note: Versions change when the UN classification it tracks is revised — 1999 to 2018 is the whole history so far; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/792 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on harmonised indices of consumer prices and the house price index, and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The HICP framework regulation: it lays down the common framework for the development, production and dissemination of the harmonised indices of consumer prices and the house price index at Union and national level, and its Annex I carries ECOICOP. Every Member State's own HICP reference metadata names it as the legal basis of its national index. Minted 2026-09-14.

reports.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1148 of 31 July 2020 laying down the methodological and technical specifications in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/792 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards harmonised indices of consumer prices and the house price index
reports.description: The act that implements the HICP framework regulation — the methodological and technical specifications the harmonised indices are actually compiled to. Named in every Member State's HICP reference metadata immediately after Regulation (EU) 2016/792. Minted 2026-09-14.

reports.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3159 of 2 September 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2016/792 of the European Parliament and of the Council on harmonised indices of consumer prices and the house price index as regards the classification of consumption and the inclusion of games of chance
reports.description: The delegated act that replaced Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2016/792 with ECOICOP version 2, aligning the European consumption classification with the revised UN COICOP and taking the divisions from 12 to 13. Its Annex states in one line that ECOICOP version 2 is identical to UN COICOP 2018. Minted 2026-09-14.

reports.title: Statistics on the production of manufactured goods (prom)
title_aliases: Statistics on the production of manufactured goods
reports.description: Eurostat's annual statistics on the production of manufactured goods, collected against the Prodcom List. Its own reference metadata states that the 8-digit Prodcom codes are derived from the 6-digit CPA headings and hence the 4-digit NACE, which is what makes it the clearest documented use of the two EU economic classifications anywhere in the corpus. Minted 2026-09-14.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the framework regulation is the instrument that carries ECOICOP — Article 2(11) defines a sub-index of the HICP as the price index for any category of ECOICOP 'as set out in Annex I', i.e. the classification is an annex to this act rather than a document it cites. Published by ECOICOP's own publisher, the European Parliament and the Council. ROUTE: EUR-Lex answers this container with an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202, zero bytes) on every legal-content URL tried, so the act was read from CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository. `http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` needs an `Accept-Language: eng` header to return anything but an error stub, and the URL cited here is the one that negotiation RESOLVES to — a `resource/cellar/<uuid>/DOC_1` document that a plain GET reads without any header at all, which is what a later grader run will issue. First-party publisher, direct read, no archive in the chain. GRADE: the grader returns B with reason `artefact-named-elsewhere-in-document` and it outranks the hand grade (PLAYBOOK 7b). The act's own full title, which is this target node's title, sits about five thousand characters above Article 2(11), outside the +/-400 character window the A bar re-runs `namesTarget` in. The quote was NOT moved to chase the grade: no span in this document both states the Annex-I relationship and carries the act's full title.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the EU act that sets the current ECOICOP states the relationship to the UN classification in one sentence in its Annex, and NAMES THE EDITION — 'UN COICOP 2018'. dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: Eurostat's own Prodcom reference metadata, section 3.2 'Classification system', states the derivation rather than an alignment — the Prodcom codes ARE CPA headings extended by two digits. This is the derivation statement PLAYBOOK 7a asks for on a nomenclature edge, and it is the first documented use of `cpa` by anything other than ESA 2010. GRADE: the grader returns B with reason `agency-not-artefact` and it outranks the hand grade (PLAYBOOK 7b). The cause is a known mechanism gap rather than the evidence: the target node's title carries its acronym as the parenthetical `(CPA)`, three characters, below the four-character floor the acronym branch of `namesTarget` applies, so a document that says `CPA` and never spells the title out cannot reach A however clearly it states the derivation. The documented remedy is `title_aliases` on the `cpa` node, which is NOT applied here — a bare three-letter `CPA` alias would also match `psab-psas`'s title, `Public Sector Accounting Standards (CPA Canada Public Sector Accounting Handbook)`, and buying one A at the price of a false one is a bad trade. Left at B deliberately.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The 8-digit codes used in the PRODCOM List are derived from the 6-digit CPA headings and hence the 4-digit NACE

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the same section of Eurostat's own Prodcom metadata, naming the NACE revision explicitly rather than 'NACE' generically — the version is what makes this citable against the `nace-rev2` node rather than a NACE-family node the corpus does not have.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14, later the same day, and the reason it was open was a READING ERROR OF MINE, not a gap in the record. The note said Eurostat's NACE Rev. 2 introductory volume 'served a 10-page cover extract rather than the full text'. It did not: `file` reports that PDF as '10 page(s)' — it misreads the linearised page tree — while `pdfinfo` reports 369 and `pdftotext` extracts all 369. The document was in hand and was written off on one tool's wrong answer. What it actually contains is the sentence the whole question needed, under its own heading 'NACE link to ISIC': 'NACE is a derived classification of ISIC'. The edge is now live at A. The original refusal of Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 as the evidence STANDS and was correct — recital 8 places a requirement on users and Annex I is a correspondence column; neither states the derivation. Kept rather than deleted so the mistake is on the record next to the thing it delayed. **Check `pdfinfo`, never `file`, before calling a PDF truncated.**

Regulation (EC) No 451/2008, the CPA's own establishing act, was read in full this round. Its only statement about an upstream classification is recital 10 — product classifications must be 'directly linked to the Central Product Classification (CPC) Ver. 2, as adopted by the United Nations Statistical Commission' — the same user-requirement shape as NACE's ISIC recital, and the corpus has no CPC node to point at. Worth recording that the regulation NEVER MENTIONS NACE: 'NACE' appears zero times in the whole act, so the CPA-to-NACE structural relationship everybody assumes is not stated by the instrument that establishes the CPA. It IS stated by Eurostat's Prodcom metadata, which is where this round's `eurostat-prodcom -> cpa` and `-> nace-rev2` edges come from. UPDATE, same day: the last sentence of this note is now understated. Eurostat's NACE Rev. 2 volume, paragraph 125, states the CPA-to-NACE relationship directly — 'with NACE as the reference framework ... the structure of CPA corresponds to NACE' — and `cpa -> nace-rev2` is wired off it at A. What stays open is only the CPC half: there is still no `cpc` node, and paragraph 125's 'CPA is the European version of the CPC' is the sentence that would carry that edge if one is ever minted.
